marrow__PHYSIO_CH43_Q001.takeaway: Maximal skeletal-muscle tension is about 3–4 kg per cm² of cross-sectional area.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH43_Q001.displayText:
Maximal skeletal-muscle tension is about 3–4 kg per cm² of cross-sectional area.

The strength of a muscle is determined mainly by its size, with a maximal contractile force between 3 and 4 kg/cm2 of muscle cross-sectional area.

• The female muscle can achieve almost exactly the same maximal force of contraction as that of the male muscle per square centimeter of cross-sectional area.
• Most of the difference in total muscle performance between males and females lies in the extra percentage of the male body that is muscle, which is caused partly by endocrine differences:
• Testosterone secreted by the male testes has a powerful anabolic effect in causing greatly increased deposition of protein in the muscles.
• Estrogen increases the deposition of fat in the female, especially in the breasts, hips, and subcutaneous tissue.
emphasis: Maximal skeletal-muscle tension is about 3–4 kg per cm² of cross-sectional area

rationales.b: 5–6 kg/cm² exceeds the standard maximal specific tension range.
rationales.c: 10–12 kg/cm² is far above typical muscle specific force.
rationales.d: 15–17 kg/cm² greatly overestimates normal maximal contractile force.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH43_Q002.takeaway: High-carbohydrate intake maximizes endurance at marathon pace by replenishing glycogen and supporting sustained oxidative metabolism.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH43_Q002.displayText:
High-carbohydrate intake maximizes endurance at marathon pace by replenishing glycogen and supporting sustained oxidative metabolism.

When athletes run at speeds typical for the marathon race, the time that they can sustain the race until complete exhaustion (also known as endurance) is maximal with a high-carbohydrate diet.

A person, who consumes a high-carbohydrate diet, stores far more glycogen in muscles than does a person who consumes either a mixed diet or a high-fat diet. Therefore, endurance is enhanced by a high-carbohydrate diet.

When athletes run at speeds typical for the marathon race, their endurance is approximately the following:
emphasis: High-carbohydrate intake maximizes endurance at marathon pace by replenishing glycogen and supporting sustained oxidative metabolism

rationales.a: High-fat diet does not provide the same glycogen availability for high-intensity endurance pace.
rationales.c: A mixed diet may sustain exercise, but the source identifies high carbohydrate as maximizing endurance.
rationales.d: Sodium intake supports electrolyte balance but does not maximize time to exhaustion.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH43_Q003.takeaway: A 100-m sprint relies primarily on the phosphagen system using stored ATP and phosphocreatine for rapid power.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH43_Q003.displayText:
A 100-m sprint relies primarily on the phosphagen system using stored ATP and phosphocreatine for rapid power.

The phosphagen system is utilized by the muscles of the athlete's body during a dash race.

The combined amounts of cell ATP and cell phosphocreatine are called the phosphagen energy system. These substances together can provide maximal muscle power for 8 to 10 seconds, almost enough for the 100-meter run. Thus, the energy from the phosphagen system is used for maximal short bursts of muscle power.

Energy systems:
• The phosphocreatine-creatine system: The combined amounts of cell ATP and cell phosphocreatine are called the phosphagen energy system. These substances together can provide maximal muscle power for 8 to 10 seconds.
• The glycogen–lactic acid system: can provide 1.3 to 1.6 minutes of maximal muscle activity.
• The aerobic system: The aerobic system is the oxidation of foodstuffs in the mitochondria to provide energy. It can sustain muscle activity for an unlimited time (as long as nutrients last).
emphasis: A 100-m sprint relies primarily on the phosphagen system using stored ATP and phosphocreatine for rapid power

rationales.b: Anaerobic glycolysis becomes more important for longer intense efforts, not the initial primary sprint system.
rationales.c: Aerobic metabolism contributes more during prolonged exercise than a short dash.
rationales.d: Pentose phosphate pathway supplies biosynthetic reducing power, not rapid muscle ATP.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH43_Q004.takeaway: Endurance slow-twitch fibers are rich in mitochondria, myoglobin and capillaries, and are smaller rather than twice the fast-fiber diameter.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH43_Q004.displayText:
Endurance slow-twitch fibers are rich in mitochondria, myoglobin and capillaries, and are smaller rather than twice the fast-fiber diameter.

Slow-twitch fibres, which are adapted for endurance running, are not larger in diameter than fast-twitch fibres. Fast-twitch fibres are about twice as large in diameter compared with slow-twitch fibres.

Fast-Twitch and Slow-Twitch Muscle Fibers
• Fast-twitch fibres can deliver extreme amounts of power from a few seconds to a minute.
• The enzymes that promote rapid release of energy from the phosphagen and glycogen–lactic acid energy systems are more active in fast-twitch fibres.
• Fast-twitch fibres are about twice as large in diameter compared with slow-twitch fibres.
• Gastrocnemius muscle has a higher preponderance of fast-twitch fibres, which gives it the capability of forceful and rapid contraction of the type used in jumping.
• Slow-twitch fibres are mainly organized for endurance, especially for the generation of aerobic energy.
• They have far more mitochondria than do the fast-twitch fibres.
• They contain considerably more myoglobin. The extra myoglobin increases the rate of diffusion of oxygen throughout the fibre.
• The enzymes of the aerobic metabolic system are considerably more active in slow-twitch fibres.
• The number of capillaries is greater in the vicinity of slow-twitch fibres.
• Soleus muscle has a higher preponderance of slow-twitch muscle fibres and therefore is used to a greater extent for prolonged lower leg muscle activity.
emphasis: Endurance slow-twitch fibers are rich in mitochondria, myoglobin and capillaries, and are smaller rather than twice the fast-fiber diameter

rationales.a: Slow-twitch fibers contain abundant mitochondria for oxidative ATP generation.
rationales.b: High myoglobin supports oxygen storage and endurance metabolism.
rationales.c: Greater capillary density supports oxygen delivery to oxidative fibers.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH43_Q005.takeaway: Joint and muscle proprioceptor input contributes to the rapid feed-forward increase in ventilation at exercise onset.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH43_Q005.displayText:
Joint and muscle proprioceptor input contributes to the rapid feed-forward increase in ventilation at exercise onset.

Signals from joint proprioceptors play a role in stimulating the respiratory drive during exercise.

Regulation of respiration in exercise
• During strenuous exercise, O2 consumption and CO2 formation can increase as much as 20-fold. Yet in the healthy athlete, the arterial PO2, PCO2, and pH remain almost exactly normal. This is because the alveolar ventilation increases along with the increased level of oxygen metabolism.
• Part of this stimulation of alveolar ventilation results from direct stimulation of the respiratory center by nervous signals. An additional part is believed to result from sensory signals transmitted into the respiratory center from the contracting muscles and joint proprioceptors.
• During strenuous exercise, the utilization of O2 in the entire body can increase to 75% to 85%. So, essentially all the oxygen is given to the exercising muscles leading to an increased arterio-venous difference in oxygen concentration.
emphasis: Joint and muscle proprioceptor input contributes to the rapid feed-forward increase in ventilation at exercise onset

rationales.b: Arterial PCO₂ is usually regulated near baseline during moderate exercise rather than rising significantly.
rationales.c: The arteriovenous oxygen difference increases as exercising muscle extracts more O₂.
rationales.d: Arterial pH is generally maintained during moderate exercise and may fall only with intense lactate accumulation.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH43_Q006.takeaway: The fall in bicarbonate is a compensatory response to altitude-induced respiratory alkalosis and is not itself the limiting factor that hinders exercise.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH43_Q006.displayText:
The fall in bicarbonate is a compensatory response to altitude-induced respiratory alkalosis and is not itself the limiting factor that hinders exercise.

The fall in blood bicarbonate levels is compensatory, and it helps increase the exercise effort, not hinder it.

Adaptation at High Altitudes
The work capacity is reduced at high altitudes and this reduction is in direct proportion to the decrease in O2 uptake. (Option B)

Immediate exposure to low PO2 at higher altitudes stimulates the arterial chemoreceptors, and this stimulation increases alveolar ventilation.

This immediate increase in pulmonary ventilation upon rising to a high altitude blows off large quantities of CO2, reducing the PCO2 and increasing the pH of the body fluids (Respiratory alkalosis). This raised pH inhibits the brain stem respiratory center and opposes the increased ventilation. So, respiratory alkalosis will hinder the maximal exercise effort. (Option C).

To compensate for this respiratory alkalosis, kidneys reduce hydrogen ion secretion and increase bicarbonate excretion. This reduces plasma and cerebrospinal fluid bicarbonate concentration and brings the pH towards normal. This removes the inhibitory effect of alkalosis on respiration. Hence the fall in blood bicarbonate facilitates the exercise effort.

NOTE
Lactic acid causes extreme fatigue. (Option D)

Ordinarily, the pyruvic acid from glycolysis enters the mitochondria of muscle cells and reacts with oxygen to form many ATP molecules.

However, when there is insufficient oxygen (at high altitudes), most of the pyruvic acid then is converted into lactic acid, which diffuses out of the muscle cells into the interstitial fluid and blood.
emphasis: The fall in bicarbonate is a compensatory response to altitude-induced respiratory alkalosis and is not itself the limiting factor that hinders exercise

rationales.b: Reduced inspired oxygen supply at altitude directly limits aerobic capacity.
rationales.c: Respiratory alkalosis initially shifts the oxygen curve left and can constrain oxygen unloading.
rationales.d: High lactate during strenuous effort contributes to fatigue and exercise limitation.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH43_Q007.takeaway: Smoking impairs exercise through airway narrowing, secretions and ciliary dysfunction; chemoreceptor desensitization is not the listed mechanism.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH43_Q007.displayText:
Smoking impairs exercise through airway narrowing, secretions and ciliary dysfunction; chemoreceptor desensitization is not the listed mechanism.

Smoking causes no change to the sensitivity of the chemoreceptors.

Effect of Smoking on Pulmonary Ventilation in Exercise
• Nicotine causes constriction of the terminal bronchioles of the lungs, which increases the resistance of air flow into and out of the lungs.
• The irritating effects of the smoke causes increased fluid secretion into the bronchial tree and some degree of swelling of the epithelial linings, which again increases airflow resistance.
• Nicotine paralyzes the cilia on the surfaces of the respiratory epithelial cells. As a result, much debris accumulates in the passageways, and this adds further to the difficulty in breathing.
• All these factors together make even a light smoker experience respiratory strain during maximal exercise, and their level of performance may be reduced.
• In persons with severe emphysema, as much as four-fifths of the respiratory membrane can be destroyed; then, even the slightest exercise can cause respiratory distress. Chronic smoking is an important cause of emphysema.
emphasis: Smoking impairs exercise through airway narrowing, secretions and ciliary dysfunction; chemoreceptor desensitization is not the listed mechanism

rationales.b: Smoking increases airway mucus and fluid secretion.
rationales.c: Smoke damages/paralyzes cilia, impairing mucociliary clearance.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH43_Q008.takeaway: Exercise increases body temperature through metabolic heat production; the listed blood pH/flow claims are not universally true.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH43_Q008.displayText:
Exercise increases body temperature through metabolic heat production; the listed blood pH/flow claims are not universally true.

Exercise causes an increase in body temperature.

Almost all the energy released by the body's metabolism of nutrients is eventually converted into body heat. Since metabolism rises significantly during exercise there is an increase in the body temperature. This increase in body temperature is significant and even lethal conditions such as heatstroke can easily develop in an athlete.

Other options:
Option A: Cerebral blood flow is “autoregulated” extremely well between arterial pressure limits of 60 and 140 mm Hg. That is, the mean arterial pressure can be increased to as high as 140 mm Hg without significant change in cerebral blood flow.
Option B: The arterial PO2, PCO2, and pH remain almost exactly normal even though during strenuous exercise, O2 consumption and CO2 formation can increase as much as 20 fold.
Option C: The increase in blood flow to exercising muscles is immediate and not after 15 minutes.
emphasis: Exercise increases body temperature through metabolic heat production; the listed blood pH/flow claims are not universally true

rationales.a: Cerebral blood flow is autoregulated and does not simply rise with systolic pressure.
rationales.b: Arterial pH is often maintained except during severe high-intensity lactate accumulation.
rationales.c: Active-muscle blood flow rises early, not only after 15 minutes.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH43_Q009.takeaway: Coronary blood flow rises during exercise to meet increased myocardial oxygen demand.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH43_Q009.displayText:
Coronary blood flow rises during exercise to meet increased myocardial oxygen demand.

Coronary circulation increases during exercise.

During exercise, blood flow
• Decreases in inactive skeletal muscles, kidney, liver, and GIT
• Remains unaltered in brain (due to autoregulation)
• Increases in exercising muscles, coronary circulation
• Initially decreases due to redistribution, but later increases due to an increase in temperature in the skin
emphasis: Coronary blood flow rises during exercise to meet increased myocardial oxygen demand

rationales.a: Cutaneous flow may rise for heat loss later, but can initially fall with sympathetic vasoconstriction.
rationales.b: Hepatosplanchnic flow typically decreases as blood is redistributed to active muscle.
rationales.d: Cerebral blood flow is relatively stable rather than markedly increased.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH43_Q010.takeaway: Exercise shifts the Hb–O₂ dissociation curve right through heat, CO₂ and acidity; a left shift is not expected.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH43_Q010.displayText:
Exercise shifts the Hb–O₂ dissociation curve right through heat, CO₂ and acidity; a left shift is not expected.

Left shift of Hb-O2 dissociation curve is not seen during exercise.

During exercise, several factors shift the Hb-O2 dissociation curve considerably to the right, thus delivering extra amounts of O2 to the active, exercising muscle fibers.

The right shift of Hb-O2 dissociation curve is due to the following:
• Release of large quantities of CO2 by the exercising muscles
• Increase in the hydrogen ion concentration in the muscle capillary blood
• Increase in the temperature of the muscle by 2° to 3°C
emphasis: Exercise shifts the Hb–O₂ dissociation curve right through heat, CO₂ and acidity; a left shift is not expected

rationales.b: Blood supply to active muscle increases during exercise.
rationales.c: Working muscle extracts more oxygen, widening the arteriovenous O₂ difference.
rationales.d: Arterial pH is often maintained in moderate exercise; this is not the false statement keyed.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH43_Q011.takeaway: Local metabolites such as adenosine, K⁺, CO₂, H⁺ and lactate dilate arterioles in active muscle and increase flow.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH43_Q011.displayText:
Local metabolites such as adenosine, K⁺, CO₂, H⁺ and lactate dilate arterioles in active muscle and increase flow.

The tremendous increase in muscle blood flow that occurs during skeletal muscle activity is caused mainly by chemicals acting directly on the muscle arterioles to cause dilation.

These chemicals include:
• Potassium ions,
• Adenosine triphosphate (ATP),
• Lactic acid, and
• Carbon dioxide.

Other factors leading to increased muscle flow include
• sympathetic nervous system activation
• increase in arterial pressure, and
• increase in cardiac output.

However, the effect of local metabolites is greater than these factors in increasing the muscle blood flow. Hence, the best answer is local metabolites.
emphasis: Local metabolites such as adenosine, K⁺, CO₂, H⁺ and lactate dilate arterioles in active muscle and increase flow

rationales.a: Raised systemic pressure is not the main local control of muscle hyperemia.
rationales.c: Sympathetic discharge constricts many peripheral beds; local metabolic vasodilation dominates in active muscle.
rationales.d: Heart rate increases cardiac output but is not the primary local vasodilator mechanism.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH43_Q012.takeaway: Static isometric exercise produces a larger rise in diastolic pressure because sustained contraction compresses vessels and raises resistance.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH43_Q012.displayText:
Static isometric exercise produces a larger rise in diastolic pressure because sustained contraction compresses vessels and raises resistance.

There is a sharp rise in the diastolic blood pressure in isometric exercise. This is due to the sustained compression of the blood vessels by the contracting muscles. In isotonic exercise, there is much vasodilatation in exercising muscles. So, even though the muscles are contracting, there is no rise in the diastolic blood pressure.

Option (a) Since the muscle pump is more active during isotonic exercise, the venous return is higher in isotonic exercise.
Option (b) The increase in the muscle blood flow is less compared to isotonic exercise since inflow of blood is obstructed by sustained compression exerted by the contracting muscle.
Option (d) Isometric exercise increases the after load of the heart leading to less increase in the stroke volume of the heart.
emphasis: Static isometric exercise produces a larger rise in diastolic pressure because sustained contraction compresses vessels and raises resistance

rationales.a: Venous return can rise in dynamic exercise via muscle pump; it is not the distinguishing larger static response.
rationales.b: Muscle blood flow increases more during dynamic isotonic exercise than sustained static contraction.
rationales.d: Stroke volume rises more with dynamic exercise and venous return than with static exercise.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH43_Q013.takeaway: Heavy exercise raises mean systemic filling pressure through venoconstriction and mobilization of blood volume.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH43_Q013.displayText:
Heavy exercise raises mean systemic filling pressure through venoconstriction and mobilization of blood volume.

The mean systemic filling pressure rises tremendously at the onset of heavy exercise.

This occurs as a result of
• The sympathetic stimulation contracts the veins.
• Tensing of the abdominal and other skeletal muscles of the body compresses many of the internal vessels, thus providing more compression of the entire vascular system and causing a still greater increase in mean systemic filling pressure.

Cardiovascular Changes in Exercise
• The maximum increase of cardiac output is 4-fold that can commonly be achieved by the untrained runner and 7-fold that can be achieved in some marathon runners.
• The increase in heart rate accounts for a greater proportion of the increase in cardiac output than the increase in stroke volume during sustained strenuous exercise.
• Exercise also causes an increased venous return due to
• Increased activity of the respiratory pump
• Increased activity of the muscular pump
• Increased venous tone due to sympathetic stimulation
• Increased blood flow from arteries to veins
• In severe exercise, there is increased systolic and mean blood pressure due to
• vasoconstriction of the arterioles and small arteries in most tissues of the body
• increased pumping activity by the heart
• a great increase in mean systemic filling pressure caused mainly by venous contraction.

As seen in the figure, point A is the resting cardiac output. On exercise, there is a rise in the mean systemic filling pressure shown on the X-axis.
• The venous return also rises which causes the cardiac output to reach point B, which is 4 times the normal resting cardiac output.
emphasis: Heavy exercise raises mean systemic filling pressure through venoconstriction and mobilization of blood volume

rationales.a: Cardiac output can rise several-fold but not generally more than tenfold in ordinary severe exercise.
rationales.b: Increases in heart rate and stroke volume both contribute; stroke volume alone is not the main source in all exercise.
rationales.d: Systolic pressure generally rises during severe dynamic exercise rather than falls.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH43_Q014.takeaway: Active-muscle hyperemia is driven by local metabolites and increased cardiac output; decreased beta-adrenergic stimulation is not a cause.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH43_Q014.displayText:
Active-muscle hyperemia is driven by local metabolites and increased cardiac output; decreased beta-adrenergic stimulation is not a cause.

During exercise, there is increased beta-adrenergic stimulation.

Medullae of the two adrenal glands secrete large amounts of norepinephrine plus epinephrine into the circulating blood during strenuous exercise. The epinephrine often has a slight vasodilator effect because it excites more of the beta-adrenergic receptors of the vessels, which are vasodilator receptors, in contrast to the alpha vasoconstrictor receptors excited especially by norepinephrine.
emphasis: Active-muscle hyperemia is driven by local metabolites and increased cardiac output; decreased beta-adrenergic stimulation is not a cause

rationales.b: Local metabolites dilate arterioles in active muscle.
rationales.c: Higher arterial pressure can contribute to increased perfusion pressure.
rationales.d: Increased heart rate raises cardiac output and supports exercise blood flow.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH43_Q015.takeaway: Strenuous exercise may cause transient hyperkalemia from muscle K⁺ efflux; hypokalemia is not the expected immediate change.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH43_Q015.displayText:
Strenuous exercise may cause transient hyperkalemia from muscle K⁺ efflux; hypokalemia is not the expected immediate change.

Strenuous exercise can cause hyperkalemia by releasing potassium from skeletal muscle.

NOTE: Exercise leads to release of endogenous opiods and is associated with mood enhancement.
emphasis: Strenuous exercise may cause transient hyperkalemia from muscle K⁺ efflux; hypokalemia is not the expected immediate change

rationales.b: Exercise can increase endogenous opioid release.
rationales.c: High-intensity exercise can produce lactic acidosis.
rationales.d: Heat and acidity shift the oxygen dissociation curve to the right.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH43_Q016.takeaway: Respiratory quotient = CO₂ production / O₂ consumption = 200/250 = 0.8.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH43_Q016.displayText:
Respiratory quotient = CO₂ production / O₂ consumption = 200/250 = 0.8.

The respiratory quotient is 0.8.

The respiratory quotient is the ratio of carbon dioxide production to oxygen utilization.

In the given question, the CO2 production is 200mL/min, while the O2 consumption is 250mL/min.

Therefore,
Respiratory quotient = 200/250 = 0.8

The respiratory quotient (RQ) is used for determining the metabolic utilization of various foods.
• When carbohydrates are metabolized with one molecule of oxygen, one carbon dioxide molecule is released. Therefore, the RQ of carbohydrates = 1.
• When fats are oxidized, for every 100 molecules of oxygen consumed, 70 molecules of CO2 are released. Therefore, the RQ of fats is 0.70.
• Similarly, the respiratory quotient for proteins is 0.80.
emphasis: Respiratory quotient = CO₂ production / O₂ consumption = 200/250 = 0

rationales.b: RQ of 1.0 corresponds to carbohydrate oxidation with equal CO₂ and O₂ volumes.
rationales.c: 1.25 exceeds the measured ratio and is not the quotient of the given values.
